title: Capacity Guard & Escrow: Error Budget Operations and Customer Remediation Process
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a standardized operational construct called 'Capacity Guard Escrow' to simplify how we compute, allocate, and remediate dedicated capacity shortfalls for Reserved/Dedicated customers. This ticket captures the SLA language, runbook, crediting algorithm, observability hooks, and customer-facing notice templates so Sales/Legal and SREs can consistently handle degraded-serving events without ad-hoc manual reconciliations.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Legal-approved contract paragraphs for Capacity Guard Escrow and proportional credit calculation included in the SLA appendix.
A2: Monitoring dashboard and alerting runbook for capacity-degradation windows implemented (links below) and validated by SRE team.
A3: Autoscaler interlock defined: when Escrow balance crosses thresholds, autoscale policy triggers (documented) and corresponding customer notices sent automatically.
A4: Example credit calculation (token-equivalent and USD-equivalent) validated against historical incidents for three customers and reviewed by Finance.
A5: Customer-facing notice templates and remediation timeline committed to product docs and sales enablement materials.
A6: End-to-end smoke test: simulate a degradation, verify detection, compute credit, generate notice draft, and create follow-up action item in support queue.
A7: Ticket contains operational playbook with explicit SLAs, windows, and escalation steps suitable for inclusion in customer contracts.
A8: Cross-team review comments resolved and sign-offs from Legal, Finance, SRE, and Sales Engineering recorded.
A9: Implementation runbook includes how credits are applied, dispute window, and monthly reconciliation process.

2025-12-02 | Agreed on 3 degradation bands: Minor (0-10% reduction), Moderate (10-30%), Severe (>30%) with escalating credit multipliers 1x/2x/4x respectively. Chosen to balance operational burden and predictable customer remediation. - Liam

contract_snippet: Capacity Guard Escrow: Redwood will maintain a capacity escrow balance for each Dedicated customer equal to the customer's committed serving units multiplied by the escrow factor in the order form. If Redwood measures a material degradation event (see 'Degradation Window' below) and verifies that dedicated capacity shortfall caused a failure to meet committed serving units, Redwood will apply Escrow Credits to the customer's invoice as defined in this section.

Degradation Window: A verified Degradation Window is any contiguous 1-hour interval during which the customer's 95th percentile serving rate across the committed region falls below 90% of the customer's committed serving units and is not caused by Customer misconfiguration or contractual exclusions.

Escrow Credit Formula (example): Credit = min(EscrowBalance, MeasuredShortfallTokens * Multiplier), where Multiplier = 1 for Minor (<=10%), 2 for Moderate (10-30%), 4 for Severe (>30%). EscrowBalance is denominated in token-equivalents and converted to invoice currency using the monthly token rate on the invoice date.

Notice & Reconciliation: Redwood will notify the customer within 72 hours of detecting a Degradation Window with a preliminary calculation. Final reconciliation and application of credits will occur within 30 days after root-cause verification. Customers may dispute calculations within a 45-day window, after which the reconciliation is final.

Remediation Commitment: For Severe degradations (Multiplier=4), Redwood will provide a post-incident mitigation plan and a one-time architectural review offered to the customer at no charge. This is non-binding and does not replace SLO crediting above.
observability_hooks: SLOs: Add 'Committed Serving Rate' SLO measured at 1m and 1h windows; thresholds: 95% for green, 90% for warning, 80% for critical.
Dashboards: 'Capacity Escrow' dashboard with per-customer escrow balances, measured serving rate, shortfall tokens, and open remediation tickets.
Alerts: Pager when escrow depletion crosses thresholds; email/Slack digest to Account Owner and SE for preliminary notices.
Traces: Link degraded requests to model variant fallbacks or autoscaler events to disambiguate root cause.
simulation_results_summary: Ran model against last 12 months of dedicated-customer telemetry (sample of 8 mid-size customers). Median projected monthly credit under Escrow model: 0.18% of committed spend. In three outlier incidents (AZ failovers) projected credits reduced estimated manual reconciliation time by 65% compared to ad-hoc refunds.

Finance validated that converting escrow token-equivalents to USD using end-of-month token rate yields stable margins; recommendation: cap monthly escrow application at 10% of committed spend to avoid outsized exposure.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers may perceive Escrow as opaque. Mitigation: Provide per-customer dashboard and monthly statements showing escrow inflows/outflows and calculation details.
Risk: Legal pushback on 'Multiplier' language. Mitigation: Provide illustrative examples and fallback to fixed-credit alternatives for negotiated enterprise deals.
Risk: Autoscaler interlock could oscillate scaling. Mitigation: Add hysteresis windows and cooldowns to policy and run chaos tests in staging.
Risk: Fraud/spoofing of shortfall signals via synthetic load. Mitigation: Tie verification to cross-region metrics and SRE manual verification step for high-value claims.
